summary: Zhao 2021 (34956436; 46 RCTs, 4,158 adults with type 2 diabetes) found berberine used alone lowered the primary glycaemic outcomes (HbA1c -0.38%, FPG -0.58, 2hPG -1.48) versus control and was not different from Western antidiabetic drugs; added to drugs it lowered HbA1c by 0.91%. Trials were mostly Chinese and open-label with high heterogeneity. Credit is limited to glycaemic support in type 2 diabetes; the 2023 umbrella review (36999891) is abstract-only.

applicability.studied_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, mostly in China, taking berberine about 0.9-1.5 g/day for 4 weeks to 6 months.

identity.chemical_form: Berberine (oral; Chinese trials, predominantly berberine tablets); salt form not uniformly stated per trial

population.description: 46 RCTs, 4,158 adults with type 2 diabetes (2,063 berberine, 2,095 control), mostly Chinese patients; sample size >=60 and duration >=4 weeks per trial.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (single-blind and open-label allowed) of berberine alone or with standard antidiabetic therapy vs placebo/none, lifestyle or active drugs; primary outcomes HbA1c, FPG and 2hPG; subgroup by treatment method.

outcomes.name: Primary (berberine used alone subgroup): HbA1c MD -0.38 (95% CI -0.49 to -0.27), FPG MD -0.58 (-0.81 to -0.35), 2hPG MD -1.48 (-2.16 to -0.79)
Berberine alone vs Western antidiabetic medicine: no significant difference in HbA1c, FPG or 2hPG
Berberine added to antidiabetic agents: HbA1c MD -0.91 (-1.25 to -0.56), FPG -1.06, 2hPG -1.34; overall pooled HbA1c -0.73

limitations: Most trials Chinese, many open-label or single-blind; only 5 reported allocation concealment/outcome-assessor blinding; high heterogeneity driven by different interventions (Results; Discussion).

Credit applies to the berberine-alone glycaemic subgroup in type 2 diabetes; adjunct-to-drug results are reported but not transferred to standalone supplement use. Not a replacement for diabetes treatment and no weight-loss or prevention claim.
Doses were mostly 0.3-0.5 g three times daily (about 0.9-1.5 g/day); outlying entries (30 mg tid to 3 g tid) are transcribed as printed and not interpreted as a threshold.
Returned decision A043: source-content hold; methods now verified from the full text. Umbrella review 36999891 is abstract-only and gets no context.
Some included-study citations lack PubMed identifiers in the source XML; retain their exact citations rather than inventing identifiers.

Historical bibliography census (not independent scoring sources; actual included-publication membership is separately bound to the inspected source table): 33024120, 32550158, 30541217, 18397984. Each intervention and comparison requires its own applicability assessment; citation in this bibliography grants no credit.

Included-study identifiers are now bound to this source's actual included-study rows/explicit inclusion references (Tables tab1 explicit included-study row citations), with live NIH title/content identity checks. They are publication pointers, not independent-cohort counts, per-primary-study scoring approvals, preparation equivalence or new efficacy evidence. Exact unindexed source citations remain retained; no missing PMID is invented.

42 included source citations have no printed PubMed identifier in this primary source; their exact citations are retained in the source-table receipt. This is a documented identifier limitation, not a fabricated identifier or an extra independent trial.

Dr. Pham's fourth ruling set (2026-10-28): tight claim; form, dose and population kept (berberine about 0.9-1.5 g/day in adults with type 2 diabetes). Glycaemic or lipid changes are not prevention of clinical events (the ruling cites 2026 ACC/AHA advice against relying on supplements for dyslipidaemia). Preparation-specific consistency rule applied: all Table 1 arms are berberine; salt form not uniformly stated.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Mostly three times daily (some twice daily) per Table 1.
dosage_forms: oral berberine tablet (trial-specific; not stated for every trial)
co_therapies: Background or comparator antidiabetic agents (metformin, sulfonylureas, sitagliptin, etc.) and lifestyle interventions in many comparisons; berberine-alone subgroup analysed separately.
dose.reported_regimen: Table 1: most commonly berberine 0.5 g tid (11 arms) or 0.3 g tid (8 arms), also 500 mg tid, 300 mg tid, 0.5 g bid, 0.6 g/d, 0.2 g tid, 0.3-0.5 g tid; outliers printed as 30 mg tid, 100 mg tid and 3 g tid; durations 4 weeks to 6 months.

normalization.basis: No scalar pooled dose; per-trial regimens retained as printed.

source_provenance.location: Methods (eligibility, primary outcomes); Results 3.1 (participants, Table 1, subgroup by treatment method, Figures 3-5); Discussion limitations
